title: DP I: Linear / 1D (Depth Pass)
relevance: High (second wave of CF-style 1D DP after frog/rob/coins/LIS/knapsack templates — Div2 C–D “state on index/value” contests)
company_notes: Decode / keyboard / broken keys: ways to type when nn is one or two presses → Constanze / Climbing Stairs family (Meta/Amazon OA clones). Adjacent constraint coloring: recolor minimum so neighbors differ → Diverse Garland / House-Robber-with-colors. Budgeted upgrades: each item needs ops[i] upgrades, total ops ≤ k, maximize value → Make Them Equal (BFS/metric + knapsack). Equal split / payroll: split array into 2 or 3 equal-sum parts → Number of Ways / Partition Equal Subset Sum contest form.

phases.goal: Confirm the candidate sees hidden-axis linear DP—same dp[i]/dp[sum]/dp[value] engine—when statements disguise the scan axis.

must_hit.point: Same engine as the base ladder (dp[i] / dp[sum] / dp[value] with local transitions), but statements hide the axis: recolor neighbors, fall trees L/R, decode n/u runs, LIS along multiples, knapsack on BFS distances, ways with an “at least one long edge” constraint, or three equal-sum pieces.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Lists several hide-the-axis skins and still names 1D index/sum/value DP with local transitions.

must_hit.point: Recognize it when a left-to-right (or value-sorted) scan has optimal substructure and n·(small state) or n√A fits.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States L→R or value-sorted scan plus that complexity fit as the membership test.

must_hit.point: OA skins: decode/keyboard ways (Constanze / Climbing Stairs; Meta/Amazon), adjacent recolor (Diverse Garland), budgeted upgrades via ops + knapsack (Make Them Equal), equal 2/3-part split (Number of Ways).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Maps the prompt to one of those four Where-it-appears skins.

probes: What makes this depth-pass linear DP rather than a plain frog/rob/coins/LIS template?
If the statement hides recolor, fall L/R, n/u decode, multiples-LIS, BFS+knapsack, or 3 equal sums, what family do you reach for?

hints.1: Ask whether the axis is disguised even though transitions stay local on an index/sum/value.
hints.2: Cue: L→R or value-sorted optimal substructure with n·(small state) or n√A; skins include recolor, trees, decode runs, multiples, BFS knapsack, long-edge ways, 3-way partition.
hints.3: Say: same dp[i]/dp[sum]/dp[value] engine; hide-axis skins as listed; recognize when a scan has OSS and n·(small state) or n√A fits; OA maps are Constanze, Garland, Make Them Equal, Number of Ways.

phases.goal: Pick the right rewrite—value/bucket axis, Fibonacci runs, last-choice states, complement counting, or BFS+knapsack—before coding.

must_hit.point: Rewrite the axis: Boredom/Delete-and-Earn style DP on value, not index—also Orac (multiples of index; dp[i]=1+max dp[j] over j∣i) and Journey Planning (a_i−i buckets / map-sum, not full LIS).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names value/index-multiples/a_i−i as the true DP axis instead of naive index LIS.

must_hit.point: Fibonacci on runs (Constanze / Decode Ways): a block of identical letters of length L has ways = F_{L+1}; multiply independent blocks; abort on forbidden letters (m/w).
must_hit.evidence_hint: States F_{L+1} per run, product over blocks, and abort on m/w.

must_hit.point: Two states beat full history: Hard problem / Fence / Garland / Basketball keep only last choice (reversed?, color, row, height-offset); never store the whole string.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says keep last choice / small state per index, not the full string history.

must_hit.point: Complement counting (k-Tree): compute all paths of weight n with edges 1..k, then subtract (or parallel-DP) paths that never use an edge ≥ d.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes all-ways then subtract/complement the no-edge-≥d case.

must_hit.point: Make Them Equal: BFS once from 1 for op-distances up to max b_i (via x+⌊x/y⌋), then one 0/1 knapsack under budget—not Dijkstra per test.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States global BFS distances then one knapsack.

probes: Before coding, is the axis index, value, multiples, or a_i−i—and do you need last-choice states, Fibonacci runs, or complement counting?
For Constanze vs Orac vs k-Tree vs Make Them Equal, which rewrite do you pick?

hints.1: Classify value/bucket rewrite vs run-Fibonacci vs last-choice vs complement vs BFS+knapsack.
hints.2: Orac/Journey rewrite the axis; Constanze uses F_{L+1} and aborts on m/w; Hard/Fence/Garland/Basketball keep last choice; k-Tree subtracts weak paths; Make Them Equal is one BFS then knapsack.
hints.3: Say: DP on value / j∣i / a_i−i; ways=F_{L+1} per run; last color/row/reverse/offset only; all weight-n paths minus no edge ≥d; BFS once from 1 then 0/1 knapsack.

phases.goal: Verify prefix range transitions, pigeonhole gating, and local raise/collapse tricks that keep the DP small.

must_hit.point: Prefix for range transitions (Candies / George and Job): dp[i][s] needs a sum of previous dp[i−1][s−x]; maintain prefix so each state is O(1); Candies range-sum transitions run in O(NK).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions prefix over prior layer so each transition is O(1), and cites O(NK) for Candies.

must_hit.point: Pigeonhole before knapsack (Modulo Sum): if n≥m then some nonempty subset ≡0 (mod m); only run O(nm) residue DP when n<m.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Checks n≥m first, else 0/1 knapsack on residues in O(nm).

must_hit.point: Local height/raise tricks (Fence Great Again): proving +0/+1/+2 suffices collapses infinite raise space to a 3-state rolling DP per post (adjacent ≠).
must_hit.evidence_hint: States only +0/+1/+2 per post and 3-state rolling DP.

must_hit.point: Number of Ways: prefix =S/3 then =2S/3 and count pairs of cuts; Array Description uses rolling dp[pos][val] under |x_i−x_{i+1}|≤1; Caesar’s Legions uses dp[n1][n2][last][run] with careful bounds.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names the S/3–2S/3 cut count and/or the rolling band / run-cap state shapes.

probes: How do you implement range-sum transitions, Modulo Sum’s pigeonhole gate, and Fence’s raise collapse?
Sketch the DP state for Candies/George, Fence (+0/+1/+2), and Number of Ways (S/3, 2S/3).

hints.1: Think prefix sums for prior-layer ranges, a cheap pigeonhole check, and shrinking raise choices.
hints.2: Candies/George: prefix → O(1) per state (O(NK) for Candies); Modulo Sum: n≥m done, else O(nm); Fence: only +0/+1/+2 → 3-state rolling.
hints.3: Say: maintain prefix of dp[i−1]; if n≥m answer yes else residue knapsack O(nm); Fence 3-state on +0/+1/+2; Number of Ways counts cut pairs at S/3 and 2S/3.

phases.goal: State when the fit is n·(small state) / n√A, when O(n log n) LIS is forced, and when prefix or pigeonhole changes the asymptotics.

must_hit.point: Depth-pass linear DP is viable when n·(small state) or n√A fits the limits.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Quotes n·(small state) or n√A as the complexity fit check.

must_hit.point: Bubble Sort Graph forces O(n log n) LIS (longest path after one bubble pass = LIS); Candies range-sum DP is O(NK) with prefixes.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Cites O(n log n) for that LIS reduction and O(NK) for Candies.

must_hit.point: Modulo Sum: O(nm) residue DP only when n<m; n≥m is immediate via pigeonhole. Prefix maintenance makes each Candies/George state O(1).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Separates the n≥m shortcut from O(nm), and O(1) per state via prefix.

probes: What complexity fit do you quote before committing to this DP family?
When is O(n log n) forced, when is Candies O(NK), and when do you skip O(nm) Modulo Sum DP?

hints.1: Separate the family fit check from the forced LIS / Candies / Modulo Sum costs.
hints.2: Fit: n·(small state) or n√A; Bubble Sort Graph → O(n log n); Candies → O(NK); Modulo Sum → O(nm) only if n<m.
hints.3: Say: n·(small state) or n√A; Bubble Sort Graph forces O(n log n) LIS; Candies O(NK) with O(1) prefix transitions; Modulo Sum pigeonhole when n≥m else O(nm).

phases.goal: Catch axis mistakes, forbidden-letter aborts, per-test BFS, and missing pigeonhole/raise collapses.

must_hit.point: Treating Orac as value-LIS or Journey Planning as full LIS: Orac is divisor-chain LIS (j∣i); Journey beauty is constant on a_i−i (map-sum).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Corrects to multiples/divisor chains and a_i−i buckets.

must_hit.point: Constanze: forgetting to abort on forbidden m/w, or wrong Fibonacci indexing on a run of length L (ways = F_{L+1}).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions abort on m/w and F_{L+1} for run length L.

must_hit.point: Make Them Equal: Dijkstra (or BFS) per test instead of one BFS from 1 up to max b_i then one knapsack.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Insists on a single precomputed distance table plus one knapsack.

must_hit.point: Modulo Sum without pigeonhole (running O(nm) when n≥m), or Fence without proving +0/+1/+2 suffices (leaving an infinite raise space).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names n≥m shortcut and the +0/+1/+2 collapse.

probes: What goes wrong if you run value-LIS on Orac, skip the m/w abort on Constanze, or BFS per test on Make Them Equal?
How do Modulo Sum’s n≥m check and Fence’s +0/+1/+2 proof save you?

hints.1: Check the true axis, forbidden letters, and whether costs were precomputed once.
hints.2: Orac=j∣i; Journey=a_i−i; Constanze abort m/w and F_{L+1}; one BFS then knapsack; n≥m pigeonhole; Fence only +0/+1/+2.
hints.3: List: not value-LIS on Orac; map a_i−i; abort m/w and use F_{L+1}; never Dijkstra/BFS per test; if n≥m done else O(nm); collapse raises to +0/+1/+2.

tradeoffs.topic: DP on value / buckets vs DP on index
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Boredom/Delete-and-Earn, Orac (multiples of index), and Journey Planning (a_i−i) move the axis to value or a bucket key; index-LIS or full-array scans miss the constant-on-bucket structure.

tradeoffs.topic: Complement counting vs direct constrained paths (k-Tree)
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Often easier to count all paths of weight n with edges 1..k, then subtract (or parallel-DP) paths that never use an edge ≥ d, instead of threading the threshold into every transition from the start.
Min changes so no two neighbors match can be a 3-state DP or a greedy recolor; both target the same adjacent-constraint coloring family.

tradeoffs.topic: DP reachability vs math cutoff (I Hate 1111)
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Unbounded coins of form (10^k−1)/9 can be solved with DP reachability or a math cutoff—same family, different proof load.

tradeoffs.topic: Pigeonhole shortcut vs O(nm) residue knapsack (Modulo Sum)
tradeoffs.strong_answer: If n≥m some nonempty subset ≡0 (mod m); only when n<m do you run the O(nm) 0/1 knapsack on residues.

tradeoffs.topic: Last-choice small state vs full history
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Hard problem / Fence / Garland / Basketball keep only last choice (reversed?, color, row, height-offset); storing the whole string is unnecessary.

gotchas.trap: Running value-LIS on Orac and Models.
gotchas.correction: Use divisor-chain LIS: dp[i]=1+max dp[j] over j∣i.

gotchas.trap: Treating Journey Planning as a full LIS.
gotchas.correction: Beauty is constant on a_i−i; map-sum the buckets.

gotchas.trap: Constanze Fibonacci decode without aborting on m/w, or wrong run formula.
gotchas.correction: Abort on forbidden m/w; a run of length L contributes F_{L+1} ways; multiply independent blocks.

gotchas.trap: Make Them Equal: shortest-path / Dijkstra (or BFS) per testcase.
gotchas.correction: BFS once from 1 for all op-distances up to max b_i, then one 0/1 knapsack.

gotchas.trap: Modulo Sum always running residue DP.
gotchas.correction: If n≥m, pigeonhole gives a nonempty subset ≡0 (mod m); else O(nm) residue knapsack.

gotchas.trap: Fence Great Again allowing arbitrary height increases.
gotchas.correction: Prove +0/+1/+2 per post suffices; then 3-state rolling DP with adjacent ≠.

gotchas.trap: Storing full string history for Hard problem / Garland / Basketball / Fence.
gotchas.correction: Keep only last choice (reversed?, color, row, height-offset).
